title: Pricing variance + privileged onboarding preflight - Nimbus Payments
next_steps: Redwood to share redline-friendly DPA + MSA excerpt link (Ben) by 2025-11-24
SE to run latency/cost micro-benchmark on customer sample workload and share results (Priya) by 2025-11-27
Nimbus legal to send list of nonstandard clauses they need for escalation (Emma) by 2025-11-25
Schedule follow-up procurement readout with finance and legal — target 2025-11-28 (Carlos)
action_items: Ben - upload security packet & SSO/KMS integration notes to shared drive (due 2025-11-24)
Priya - run 100K token/day cost projection for hosted vs dedicated (due 2025-11-26)
Leah - supply their internal data classification matrix for egress mapping (due 2025-11-25)
Emma - circle back with contract team on escrow/indemnity ask (due 2025-12-01)
summary: Procurement/legal handoff call focused on pricing variance, privileged onboarding (KMS/SSO), and acceptance criteria for a short pilot. Redwood AE + SE paired; customer procurement + infosec + legal present. Discussed hosted vs dedicated economics, SLA expectations, data residency and KMS options. Agreed concrete next steps: send DPA redline guidance, run micro-benchmarks, and schedule legal follow-up.
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-20 14:00 UTC | Duration 42m 
Attendees: Ben Holloway (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Hassan Ali (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendes (Nimbus Procurement), Leah Park (Nimbus Infosec), Rajiv Kapoor (Engineering Manager), Emma Stone (Legal), Marta Ruiz (Product)

[00:00] Ben: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have a packed agenda, quick intros?
[00:12] Carlos: yep carlos from procurement, i'll be owning the pricing and contracting path, thanks for the invite
[00:18] Leah: leah, infosec, i'll focus on dpa and keys, hi
[00:21] Rajiv: rajiv eng, we'll own the pilot run and perf validation
[00:24] Emma: emma legal, i'll be the contract contact
[00:27] Ben: awesome, ben from redwood, priya is our se for technical deepdive and hassan on onboarding

[01:05] Ben: quick outline — we want to align on the pricing variance you flagged, privileged onboarding (kms + sso), and get a path for legal redlines, plus next steps for a pilot
[01:20] Marta: quick point — product wants to know if latency SLOs are realistic for our 99th percentile with our 1k concurrent users pattern

[02:00] Priya: just to set expectations, our hosted API latency profile for 'medium' open models at N=1 is typically 60-120ms p50 and 300-500ms p95 depending on sequence length; dedicated pools tighten that substantially — p95s in 120-180ms range for comparable batch sizing
[02:32] Rajiv: ok, curious how much of that changes when you enable prefix caching and if we use 8-bit quantized variants
[02:45] Priya: prefix/KV caching helps a lot for repeated context, quantization trades a bit of quality for ~20-40% cost savings and sometimes lower latency; we'll run a micro-benchmark with your sample workload to show numbers

[04:12] Carlos: on pricing — procurement sees the base on-demand rates but the pricing team needs committed tiers to hit our model for the quarter. what's realistic for a 6-12 month commit?
[04:30] Ben: we typically offer graduated discounts at commit bands; example: 3-5% for small commit, 10-18% for mid, 20%+ for enterprise-level reserved capacity. but dedicated capacity is contracted differently — fixed monthly capacity with throughput guarantees
[04:58] Carlos: any egress or KMS add-on fees we should model?
[05:10] Hassan: standard egress to public internet is accounted, cross-region egress and HSM key escrow have separate fee lines; we'll provide a pricing sheet with line items — i'll attach that after the call (link: /shared/pricing/nimbus-draft.xlsx)

[06:25] Emma: on the MSA/DPA side, we have three asks: indemnity cap clarification, data deletion timelines, and an audit access window. is Redwood ok with a 45-day purge timeline for transient PII used in evals?
[06:40] Ben: purge timelines are negotiable; our standard is 30 days for transient logs but we can accommodate 45 if necessary — i can flag that for legal
[06:52] Emma: also we need KMS integration details — can customer manage keys (BYOK) or is escrow required?
[07:05] Priya: both options supported. Hosted can integrate with customer's cloud KMS via customer-managed keys; for Dedicated and Private we support both customer KMS and HSM appliances. For BYOK there's an ingestion/rotation window we document in the security pack

[08:20] Leah: does that require privileged network paths? i'm worried about lateral access and privileged user controls
[08:30] Priya: when using customer-managed KMS we require a tight RBAC mapping and least-privilege service principal; for private deployments you can lock it down to VPC-only subnets and we support IP allowlists, SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning

[09:45] Rajiv: can we get a topology diagram? we need to show how tokens flow, where KV cache lives, and what telemetry is sent back to Redwood
[09:55] Hassan: yes, topology + telemetry spec will be part of the security packet (we'll upload to the drive)

[11:10] Carlos: back to pricing — if we do a pilot that's internal-only for 4 weeks, can you provide a short-term discounted trial and a path to roll into committed pricing without a restart fee?
[11:25] Ben: yes, we do flexible pilots; we'd credit pilot usage against a subsequent commit in most cases — details in the pilot term sheet
[11:40] Carlos: and SLA remedies? finance wants clear credits tied to p95 latency breaches and availability drops
[11:53] Priya: our hosted SLA is availability-based with uptime credits; dedicated can have latency SLO add-ons with remedies, but we negotiate latency SLO thresholds in the dedicated contract because it depends on model variant and sequence lengths

[13:05] Emma: on data residency — some of our payment data can't leave eu-west-1. are you able to guarantee region-specific hosting?
[13:18] Ben: yes, region pinning is supported for hosted for GA regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private which you can place into your cloud region or on-prem

[14:40] Leah: audit logs — need to confirm retention and format, we require immutable audit logs for privileged sessions for 12 months
[14:55] Priya: audit log retention configurable; we can provide syslog/S3 export and append-only store for privileged sessions — we'll include retention matrix in the packet

[16:20] Rajiv: technical question — how do rollbacks work on model rollouts? if you do a canary rollout and quality regresses, what's the fallback path?
[16:33] Priya: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous pinned model; we can also do A/B tests and route percentage of traffic. For Dedicated we isolate deployment groups so rollbacks are instant and traffic diverted to fallback node pools

[18:05] Marta: acceptance criteria for the pilot — product needs latency <= 250ms p95 on average workloads and no more than 5% inference cost delta vs our baseline within 4 weeks
[18:20] Priya: we'll design the pilot harness to capture those metrics and instrument the KV cache/seq lengths to be representative

[19:50] Carlos: procurement will need a final pricing worksheet and the proposed MSA+DPA redline before we route to finance — timeline target end of next week if possible
[20:03] Ben: that's doable. we'll send DPA redline guidance and a redline-friendly excerpt of MSA; we'll flag cross-walks for indemnity and data deletion

[21:30] Emma: caveat — we may have an escrow/escrow agent ask around model weights for certain regulatory reasons; not sure yet but want to pre-flag
[21:42] Ben: noted; we tend to handle escrow on enterprise contracts, let's capture the requirement and loop legal

[22:55] Leah: one more security question — SOC2/ISO evidence, do you publish attestation reports and can they be shared under NDA?
[23:06] Hassan: yes we publish SOC2 type II and ISO27001 certificates; we can share the redacted reports under NDA, and the security packet will include control mappings

[24:40] Rajiv: for the performance micro-benchmark, we'll share a 10-20k token/day sample trace — what's the recommended tokenization and dataset format?
[24:52] Priya: a gzip of newline-delimited prompts and an expected response set is ideal; we can ingest as JSONL and run approx 2k prompts at various seq lengths to mirror production; we'll return latency histograms and cost per 1k tokens

[26:30] Carlos: competitors — we're also looking at MegaCloud AI because they offered lower headline rates but fewer private deployment options. how do you advise us versus them?
[26:44] Ben: MegaCloud's rates can be lower on purely on-demand pricing but often they don't provide the same observability or private deployment flexibility; Redwood's differentiation is auditable SLAs, dedicated pools, and clear cost levers like batching and caching that reduce unit economics

[28:10] Emma: contract redlines — our legal will want to remove "most favored nation" or add carveouts; we may request a 24 month renewal cap but that's negotiable
[28:23] Ben: we'll note the MFN ask; our commercial team usually scopes renewal caps in enterprise schedules

[29:50] Priya: small technical note — for key rotation with BYOK there's a short outage window (~30-90s) while KV caches refresh; we'll document recommended rotation windows and orchestration steps

[31:15] Leah: can we do SCIM for provisioning? we need automated deprovisioning when people leave
[31:26] Hassan: yes SCIM + SAML supported, we can show sample SCIM mappings in the onboarding doc

[33:00] Marta: regarding billing granularity — can finance get token-level line items and per-route breakdowns?
[33:12] Ben: yes, the console exposes per-route and per-token breakdowns and we can export CSVs for FinOps consumption

[34:40] Carlos: to summarize procurement asks: 1) definitive pricing worksheet with commit bands 2) pilot credits applied to commit 3) DPA/MSA redline sent to Emma 4) timeline for legal signoff — can we aim for 3 weeks?
[34:56] Ben: yes we'll aim to get the materials in the next 4 business days, target legal signoff in ~3 weeks if no major redlines

[36:10] Emma: will there be a negotiation on SLA remedies? want to make sure it's not purely credit-based for latency breaches
[36:22] Ben: for certain enterprise customers we can discuss bespoke remedies; we typically default to credits but can explore alternate remedies on case-by-case

[37:40] Priya: technical checklist for pilot — we'll need: service account access for test env, sample prompt corpus, expected acceptance metrics, and network egress details

[38:05] Rajiv: i'll send a skeleton acceptance doc after this call with the metrics and sample dataset pointer
[38:12] Rajiv: (sigh) we'll also list which models we want to compare

[39:30] Hassan: i'll create a shared folder and drop the security packet, pricing sheet, and pilot playbook — link will be in the follow-up email

[40:05] Ben: ok final recap — ben will send DPA redline guidance and pilot commercial terms; priya runs micro-benchmark and perf readout; hassan uploads security packet and pricing spreadsheet; emma/leah/carlos to consolidate internal asks and confirm timeline. any other items?
[40:40] Emma: none from legal, thanks
[40:45] Leah: nothing further
[40:48] Carlos: good, thanks all
[40:51] Ben: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email and links — talk soon
[41:05] (meeting ends)
